correctness.rationale: I verified the uniform result with a separate exact certificate: /workspace/prism_independent_replay.py encodes ordered vertex-state pairs, composes the rule twice on every five-column word, and obtains the 23 possible adjacent time-two pairs by exhausting every six-column input. It checks all 1,491 five-column walks in that pair relation, none of which can produce an excited center two steps later. Every actual time-two cone is among these walks, even for wrapped rings, so no site is excited at time four and time five is all-rest. Direct enumeration of the three small rings gives exact maximum four with respectively 24, 336, and 3,380 first hits at four. For the stated six- and seven-column witnesses, the check gives an excited upper vertex at column 3 at time three; for n>7 the central radius-three cone is unchanged. All results concern synchronous updates with distinct open-neighborhood neighbors. I did not run the uploaded verifier; its output is frozen recorded evidence.

evidence: Using trigger positions −3,…,3: modulo 3, −2 and +1 coincide but require disjoint symbol sets; modulo 4, −3 and +1 conflict; modulo 5, −3 and +2 conflict. Thus on n=3,4,5 no excited vertex can remain at time three, and all rest follows at time four. For n=6 the repeated endpoints −3,+3 have identical allowed sets; for n≥7 all seven trigger slots can be freely filled. Such a trigger gives an excited time-three vertex and hence sharp time five.

For the remaining lower bounds, two-step excited vertices are supplied simply by row pairs (001,011) on n=3 and (0001,1010) on n=4; two direct updates give upper rows 120 and 2120, respectively. The exact ten-vertex census supplies sharpness on n=5 (also witnessed by row pair (00001,01010)).
